teams.heading: Fiji anchors the international standings after suffering three consecutive defeats
teams.body: Fiji sit 12th in the standings after failing to secure a victory in their opening three matches. The side compiled three defeats from those three fixtures. Across those three games, the team scored 49 points and conceded 145 points, resulting in a point difference of minus 96. In the third round, they suffered a 17-33 defeat against Scotland. It remains a stark contrast to 2023, when the team reached its highest ever world ranking of No. 7.

teams.heading: Maro Itoje credits summer sabbatical for refreshing mindset ahead of new season
teams.body: England captain Maro Itoje has defended his decision to miss the summer Nations Championship fixtures, describing the "mini-sabbatical" as a vital period for mental and physical recovery. The 31-year-old, who watched the July tests from afar, believes the proactive approach will help prolong his career ahead of the 2027 World Cup. "I don’t regret it at all," Itoje stated regarding the break, which was offered by Steve Borthwick following a busy professional and personal year.

teams.heading: George Skivington rules out Ross Byrne's Munster move despite Jack Crowley injury
teams.body: George Skivington has dismissed speculation that Ross Byrne will return to Ireland to join Munster as injury cover. Links to the province emerged after Jack Crowley was ruled out until the new year with a lower limb vascular injury. The Gloucester head coach insists the 31-year-old fly-half remains central to his plans, stating: 'Nobody wants him doing that role (the backup), that's not what we brought him in for.' Crowley's absence leaves Ireland's No. 10 options thin for November’s tests against Argentina, Fiji, and South Africa.

teams.heading: Gonzalo Quesada will miss South Africa clash following two-Test World Rugby suspension
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada will be absent for the November opener against South Africa after being handed a two-Test suspension. The Argentine is the first person sanctioned under World Rugby’s new Match Official Abuse Sanctioning Process following his criticism of referee Luc Ramos. The ban, which saw Quesada barred from the stadium during the recent loss to Australia, extends to the upcoming Springboks fixture. He remains prohibited from all match-day proceedings, though he retains the right to appeal the independent panel’s ruling.

lead.why: The head coach’s suspension for the upcoming South Africa Test is the most significant development affecting the national squad.

teams.heading: Former Wales players to continue concussion legal battle after High Court ruling
teams.body: The High Court has ruled that the landmark brain injury litigation brought by hundreds of former players can proceed, despite recent warnings that the case faced potential collapse. This legal action, involving several retired Wales internationals, remains in a delicate balance as the court assesses claims regarding the sport's handling of head injuries. While the decision allows the proceedings to move forward, no final judgment or collective settlement has been reached, leaving the long-term safety protocols for the professional game under intense scrutiny.

teams.heading: Nicolás Roger earns fly-half start as Santiago Carreras moves to full-back
teams.body: Argentina look to salvage their home series in Mendoza with a significant tactical reshuffle. Nicolás Roger earns a promotion to the starting fly-half role, a move that pushes Santiago Carreras to full-back. The pack also sees a complete overhaul in the engine room, where Efraín Elías and Franco Molina form an entirely new second-row combination. After a narrow defeat in the opening Test, Los Pumas aim to improve a record that has seen them win only three of their last 10 home matches.

teams.heading: Les Kiss recalls Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii as Tom Wright reaches 50 caps
teams.body: Head coach Les Kiss has made nine alterations to his starting side for the Mendoza rematch with Argentina. Midfielder Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii returns to the XV alongside Len Ikitau, while full-back Tom Wright hits a half-century of Test appearances. Kiss has opted for Ben Donaldson at flyhalf, relegating Carter Gordon to the bench as part of a strategic rotation. Reflecting on the plan, Kiss noted: “We’ve brought in some fresh bodies alongside some existing combinations as we continue to look to build Test experience.”

teams.heading: Springboks expect All Blacks to maintain high-tempo, ball-in-hand attacking approach
teams.body: South Africa assistant coach Mzwandile Stick has confirmed the Springboks are bracing for an expansive All Blacks performance in Saturday’s series decider. Despite the threat of rain in Johannesburg, Stick noted that Dave Rennie’s side refuses to play “hide and seek” with their tactical identity. By prioritising ball-in-play time and selecting mobile, dynamic forwards like Asafo Aumua and Peter Lakai, New Zealand aims to continue the high-tempo game that saw them outscore the world champions four tries to three last week.

teams.heading: Siya Kolisi urges South Africa to channel Soweto’s historic fighting spirit
teams.body: Captain Siya Kolisi has challenged his side to draw inspiration from the historical significance of Soweto ahead of Saturday’s encounter with New Zealand. Acknowledging the weight of the FNB Stadium's location, Kolisi reflected on the 1976 Soweto Uprising as a pivotal moment in the nation’s history. “So many heroes have come from there,” Kolisi noted, emphasising that the squad views the fixture as an opportunity to honour the sacrifices that shaped modern South Africa while aiming to secure a vital series advantage.
